_note: I044: corrections to stale statements found while writing docs/code/actor-system.md. Evidence: RunActors loads actor_list_tail and NextActor loads $3E, so run order is tail to head along $3E; SpawnActorAfter sets new.$3E = X and X.$3C = new (the new actor sits before X in run order, first run next frame); SpawnActorBefore sets new.$3C = X and X.$3E = new (right after X, same frame); SpawnPlacementList links every actor as the new head; the run order of the player helpers in player_core (WatchForLevelUp, RunSoulOrb, FilterPlayerInput, player, RunWeaponLayer, FinishPlayerMove) agrees. data_scene_placements: rg over the 97 lists finds 93 rows with meta type 0 and four lists whose first row is not type 0 (A00S09 type $53; A00S0A, A00S0B, A00S0C one row each, types $56, $57, $5B). RespawnOrKillActor: rg for stores into $1A in extracted/ finds only bits $0080, $0100, $0200, $0400, $0800, $2000, $4000 and $8000, never $1000. Open points: questions/I044_questions.md.

edit.with: ($3C points toward the tail = earlier in run order, $3E toward the head = later; actor_list_tail $06A6 runs first, actor_list_head $06A8 last)

edit.find: link a new actor after (SpawnActorAfter) or before (SpawnActorBefore) the caller
edit.with: link a new actor on the $3C side of the caller (SpawnActorAfter: the new actor runs before the caller, first on the next frame) or on the $3E side (SpawnActorBefore: it runs right after the caller, in the same frame)

edit.find: Sees: a monster, effect, projectile or pickup appears next to its spawner.
edit.with: Sees: a monster, effect, projectile or pickup appears next to its spawner; it sits before X in run order, so its first run is the next frame.
($3C toward the tail, $3E toward the head; the tail $06A6 runs first)

edit.find: Why: actor list order decides who runs first; after = later.
edit.with: Why: the actor loop runs from the tail along $3E, and the new actor is linked on the $3C side of the caller, so it runs before the caller and first on the next frame (the player's input filter and level-up watcher use it to run ahead of the hero).

edit.find: Why: see Cop84; before = runs earlier.
edit.with: Why: the new actor is linked on the $3E side of the caller, so it runs right after the caller in the same frame (the player's weapon layer and move finisher use it to run after the hero).

comments.24337: Unlink from the list: $3C = toward the tail (earlier in run order), $3E = toward the head; no $3C neighbour means the actor is the tail

edit.find: A new actor is linked in as the new head.
edit.with: A scene's placement list links each actor in as the new head, so its first row is the tail and runs first; SpawnActorAfter links on the $3C side of its caller (the new actor runs before the caller, first on the next frame) and SpawnActorBefore on the $3E side (right after the caller, in the same frame).

edit.find: re-creates it in the same slot from its placement record ($3A).
edit.with: re-creates it in the same slot from its placement record ($3A). No code in extracted/ sets $1A bit $1000, so by static reading the respawn branch is never taken (OQ-I044-6).

edit.find: Sees: the enemy is gone; a respawning enemy returns as a fresh copy after the player has left it off screen for about 10 seconds.
edit.with: Sees: the enemy is gone. With $1A bit $1000 set it would return as a fresh copy after the player has left it off screen for about 10 seconds; no code in extracted/ sets that bit (OQ-I044-6), so by static reading every enemy without a lair is killed here.

edit.find: Why: ordinary field enemies come back, scripted ones (and bosses) do not; $1A bit $1000 decides.
edit.with: Why: $1A bit $1000 is the switch between a field enemy that comes back and a scripted actor or boss that does not.

edit.find: The first row of every list is the hero (meta type 0): its tile is the start position of the scene when no warp_dest is set.
edit.with: The first row of 93 of the 97 lists is the hero (meta type 0): its tile is the start position of the scene when no warp_dest is set. The four lists without a hero are PlacementA00S09 (first row type $53) and PlacementA00S0A, PlacementA00S0B and PlacementA00S0C (one row each, types $56, $57 and $5B); by static reading these are the scenes of locations $0F-$12, which have no player (OQ-I044-5).

edit.with: 913 rows in all (93 hero rows and 820 other actors)
